found.notes: Steady synthetic tone, fundamental ~242 Hz with odd harmonics 721/1200/1685/2164/2649 Hz (square-wave-like), on 33.98-37.45 s and 37.7-39.3 s of the source (short ~0.25 s gap). Spectrally matches a ~250 Hz square-wave F-16 warning tone (FlightGear F-16 models its gear-horn/low-speed tone as 250 Hz square: f16nvc__250hz-square*.wav); the -3% offset could be HUD-tape speed error. Occurs seconds after the Auto-GCAS fly-up at very high airspeed, so a low-speed/gear-horn trigger is implausible; identity unknown. Cannot listen: evidence is spectral only. Alternative explanation: a radio heterodyne/squeal (two UHF transmitters keyed together right after the instructor's "recover" calls) that became square-like through the heavy clipping of this recording (symmetric clipping produces exactly these odd harmonics). Treat as unidentified; do NOT label it as an F-16 warning without listening. Harmonic analysis (37.8-39.0 s of source): f0 240.8 Hz; odd harmonics h3 -9.5 dB, h5 -16.0, h7 -20.3, h9 -25.4, h11 -28.3 dB re h1; even harmonics -37 to -50 dB — i.e. a near-ideal square wave (ideal h3 = -9.54 dB). The tone sits at ~-3.7 dBFS RMS, i.e. it is NOT clipped in this file, which argues for a synthetic tone-generator source (aircraft aural tone) rather than clipping of a radio heterodyne. Confidence that it is an F-16 aural warning tone: low-to-medium; which warning: unknown.

real_messages.fact: The F-16 Fighting Falcon voice warning system uses a female voice ("Bitching Betty"); Wikipedia also claims (flagged "non-primary source needed") that Erica Lane voiced the F-16 and AH-64 systems.

F-16 Auto-GCAS (fielded fleet-wide from 2013) executes an automatic recovery when terrain impact is imminent, based on a continuous comparison of a predicted trajectory with an onboard terrain-elevation profile; developed by NASA Armstrong, Lockheed Martin and AFRL. (No aural cue described in the article.)

Real 2016 Arizona ANG F-16 Auto-GCAS save HUD tape: audio shows pilot breathing, instructor radio calls "Two, recover" (x4) and "knock it off", plus a ~242 Hz square-wave tone after the fly-up; no voice "PULL UP"/"ALTITUDE" was detectable in the released cut.
UH-60M/HH-60M crews train high-altitude/degraded-visual-environment (dust) landings at HAMETS; the aircraft is described as "the HH-60 Mike and the UH-60 Mike model" (no alert list given).

USAARL airworthiness test reports for medical equipment on the UH-60 list the UH-60 warning systems checked for interference: "Low rotor RPM. X. Master caution. X. Caution advisory. X. Fire warning. X. AFCS. X." (UH-60A/L era; reference TM 55-1520-237-10). Quoted from DTIC search-result snippet; PDF not retrievable during research (DTIC maintenance page).

Same warning-system list ("Low rotor RPM ... Master caution ... Caution advisory ... Fire warning ... AFCS") in the USAARL test of a defibrillator in the "UH-60 and EH-60 helicopter", citing TM 55-1520-237-10 with changes 1-5 (DTIC snippet).

Army Flightfax (April 2001) mishap narrative: "As the Low Rotor RPM continued to sound, CW3 ... took command of the flight controls and executed a descending right turn" — i.e. the low-rotor-RPM warning is an aural (sounding) alert (DTIC snippet).
USAARL "Communication and Noise Hazard Survey of CH-47D Crewmembers" compares to UH-60 cockpit noise and names aural "warning signals (e.g., low rotor RPM)" (DTIC snippet).

AH-1S external-fuel study: "the low rotor rpm warning system provided an audio cue approximately 1 second following the power loss" (Army helicopter low-rotor audio cue timing; not UH-60, DTIC snippet).

search_log.key_observation: DVIDS cockpit videos rarely carry intercom audio: most cockpit b-roll is recorded by a GoPro ambient mic (engine/wind only) or has music, and some pages state explicitly "*Audio was not cleared for release*" (e.g. 723256, F-16 simulator b-roll). Where ICS audio exists (incentive rides, Thunderbird hometown-hero flights, Guard hoist rescues) no F-16 VMS words, F-22 ICAWS words, or UH-60 warning tones/voices were detected by whisper-small + tonal-track scan + spectrogram inspection. Of 325 DVIDS audio tracks downloaded, 12 were digital silence (audio stripped, e.g. 723256, 731345/731362 F-16 drone-shoot HUD, 809567), and whisper found real speech in only ~40% — mostly narration/interviews.
